html:
The Coast Miwok are a Native people of what are now Marin County and southern Sonoma County, California, north of the Golden Gate. They are one of the Miwok peoples.

They lived in villages by the bays and lagoons, eating acorns, shellfish, salmon and game. In 1579 Francis Drake probably landed among them at Drake's Bay and stayed several weeks. From the 1780s they were drawn into the missions at San Francisco and later San Rafael (1817) and Sonoma.

Their descendants, joined with the Southern Pomo, form the Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria. Other neighbours include the Kashaya Pomo and the Lake Miwok.
